verdicts.question: What type of roof is present at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Pages 5-19 (Material Delivery Route, Proposed PV Area, Cable Routing, Site Layout, 3D panel-layout renders, Building Exterior) all show a bare, flat, poured-concrete terrace slab with exposed vertical rebar stubs and no tiles or metal sheeting.

verdicts.rationale: The photographed reinforcement bars sticking up from the slab directly match the designer's stated obstruction.

verdicts.question: What is the angle of the panels? (in degrees)

verdicts.rationale: These are design-intent CAD renders (not as-built photos of an installed structure), so an exact 10° tilt cannot be visually measured; the shallow leg-height difference is only broadly consistent with a low tilt angle.

verdicts.question: What type of mounting structure is planned?

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run — from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel — with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target — the vision routine verifies it by tracing cables across photos with 'Cable Routing', 'Equipment Location', 'Meter Box' and similar captions on pages 4+.
verdicts.photo_observation: Tracing the color-coded overlay lines: an LA marker and orange LA cable on the roof (page 11) continues down the exterior wall corner across pages 11-14, reaching an AC Earth Pit marker (page 17) and, separately, a DC Earth Pit / LA Pit pair (page 16). Inside, the Inverter/ACDB/DCDB and Battery markers (pages 13, 15) connect via red/green/purple lines to a wall penetration captioned 'Make a hole to run the DC Cable, AC earthing cable up to the earth pit location', and a separate short purple line links a 'Main Meter' and 'Solar Meter' box outline (page 16). No colored line appears to start or stop without continuing onto an adjacent page's photo at a matching wall/position.
verdicts.rationale: The routing photos are a designer-drawn planning overlay on an as-yet-unbuilt site (no meter, no inverter, no cabling actually installed yet), not as-built photos of installed cable runs, so there is no physical conduit/cable-tie/clipping to visually confirm even though the overlaid path itself traces continuously with no orphan segments.
